rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Petrol is highly flammable and releases vapour that can ignite and cause serious fire or explosion.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Petrol storage at filling stations is covered by the Petroleum (Consolidation) Regulations 2014 and workplace use is also covered by DSEAR.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: A workplace with petrol dispensing equipment similar to a filling station requires a petroleum storage certificate.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Workplace filling, storage and use of approved petrol containers remain subject to DSEAR risk assessment and risk minimisation duties.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: The petrol-consolidation rules distinguish workplaces that dispense petrol from workplaces that only store it.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Users should follow filling-station safety instructions when filling a vehicle tank or portable container.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Petrol can give off flammable vapour even at very low temperatures.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Workers should remove petrol or oil contamination from skin promptly and wash properly with soap and water.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Petrol risk depends on stored quantity, container or tank integrity, transfer method, vapour control, ignition sources, drainage, traffic and supervision.

rows.source: HSE petrol storage and filling-station safety
rows.verified: Petrol evidence is site-, storage-, dispensing-, container-, task- and weather-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Commercial solid-fuel appliances such as tandoori ovens, charcoal grills and wood-fired pizza ovens can expose workers and the public to carbon monoxide.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Employers using solid-fuel cooking appliances must control carbon-monoxide exposure and comply with applicable health and safety law.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Gas-fired catering appliances, flues, pipework and safety devices must be maintained in a safe condition.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Commercial kitchens need adequate ventilation designed for the appliances, heat and combustion products present.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Ventilation duties involve caterers, building managers, designers and equipment installers when new systems are installed.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Hospitality and catering employers must ensure gas appliances, flues, pipework and safety devices are safely maintained.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Unsafe gas combustion or inadequate ventilation can create carbon-monoxide and fire risks in catering premises.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Carbon-monoxide controls must protect both employees and members of the public.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Kitchen carbon-monoxide risk depends on fuel, appliance condition, flue performance, ventilation, room volume, operating pattern, maintenance and occupancy.

rows.source: HSE commercial-kitchen gas and carbon-monoxide controls
rows.verified: Commercial-kitchen evidence is appliance-, fuel-, ventilation-, premises- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level poisoning probability.
